response.explanation: The Subscription domain class imports the SystemClock outbound adapter (src/domain/subscription.ts:1). It also creates its own instance in a private field (line 4) and calls clock.now() inside isActive() (line 9) to compare the current time with endsAt. So the domain core is tied to a concrete infrastructure adapter. Its active/inactive logic can't be driven by a substitute time source, and the dependency runs from the core out to the adapter layer instead of inward. FF-P06 flags this because a domain class holds an infrastructure type through a FLOWS_TO edge (the clock field). Accepted ADR-0009 says the core must not import SystemClock and should depend on a Clock port in src/domain that the adapter implements. ADR-0002 allowed the direct import, but ADR-0009 has superseded it, so that permission no longer applies. The fix is small and clear: define a Clock port in src/domain, have SystemClock implement it, and inject the port into Subscription instead of creating the adapter inside it.
